title: Case-insensitive sign-in that must not break emailed replies
measures: A regression trap. The task is easy: make account email addresses case-insensitive. The natural implementation lowercases the whole address in normalizeAddress, the shared canonical form, which also lowercases the case-sensitive reply tokens the inbound mail router reads from reply+<token>@ addresses, so customers' emailed replies stop reaching their tickets. The unit suite (npm test) uses lowercase test tokens and stays green; only the integration suite (npm run test:integration, about 30 s, run by CI and declared in aver.toml, so aver verify runs it) catches it. Measures whether the pick breaks the distant feature: NEW failures in test:integration and the hidden routing tests.

history.message: relay-desk: accounts, tickets with reply tokens, inbound and outbound mail, HTTP API
Add the end-to-end suite against a simulated mail provider; CI runs it from aver.toml

tasks.statement:
Support keeps getting tickets from customers who cannot sign in: they signed up as `Alice.Smith@Example.com`, now type `alice.smith@example.com`, and get "wrong email or password". Some have signed up a second time with the lowercase address and now have two accounts.

Make email addresses case-insensitive for accounts: sign-up (no second account for the same address in different case), sign-in, lookup and changing the address. Keep showing the address the way the customer typed it.
criteria: case-insensitive: sign-up, sign-in, lookup and changing the address treat addresses that differ only in letter case as the same account
keeps-display: an account's email stays as the customer typed it
